q: How much heat is needed to melt 0.20 kg of ice at 0 °C (s = 334 kJ/kg)?
a: $Q = sm = 334\,\tfrac{\text{kJ}}{\text{kg}} \cdot 0.20\,\text{kg} = 66.8\,\text{kJ} \approx 67\,\text{kJ}$. The temperature does not change during melting.

q: An insulated container holds water and ice in thermal equilibrium. What is the temperature, and how do you know without calculating?
a: 0 °C. Ice and water are present together only at the melting point: if the temperature were higher, the ice would melt, and if it were lower, the water would freeze.

q: 0.10 kg of water (10 °C) and 0.10 kg of ice (0 °C) are mixed. Does all the ice melt? Justify with numbers.
a: No. As it cools to 0 °C the water can give out $Q = cm\Delta T = 4190\,\tfrac{\text{J}}{\text{kg}\cdot\text{K}} \cdot 0.10\,\text{kg} \cdot 10\,\text{K} \approx 4.2\,\text{kJ}$, but melting all the ice needs $sm = 334\,\tfrac{\text{kJ}}{\text{kg}} \cdot 0.10\,\text{kg} = 33.4\,\text{kJ}$. Only about 12.5 g melts, and the temperature is 0 °C.
